Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_ollama-gemma4-31b_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_ollama-gemma4-31b_01.html`.

{"edit_description":"Implement the full CHIP-8 instruction set within the `step()` method of the `Chip8` class. 
Ensure all 35 instructions are covered, including:
- 00E0: Clear screen
- 1NNN: Jump to address NNN
- 2NNN: Call address NNN
- 3XNN: Skip if VX == NN
- 4XNN: Skip if VX != NN
- 5XNN: Skip if VX == NN (some variants)
- 6XNN: Set VX to NN
- 7XNN: Add NN to VX
- 8XY0: Set VX to VY
- 8XY1: Set VX to VX XOR VY
- 8XY2: Set VX to VX AND VY
- 8XY3: Set VX to VX OR VY
- 8XY4: Set VX to VX + VY (with carry in VF)
- 8XY5: Set VX to VX - VY (with borrow in VF)
- 8XY6: Set VX to shift right VY (or VX)
- 8XY7: Set VX to shift left VY (or VX)
- 9XNN: Jump if VX == NN
- ANNN: Set I to NNN
- AXNN: Set VX to BCD of VX
- CXNN: Set VX to number of keys pressed
- DXNN: Set index I to X in keypad
- EXNN: Set VX to value of key NN
- FX00: Set I to PC
- FX01: Set PC to I
- FX15: Set I to VX
- FX18: Set VX to value at address I
- FX1E: Set VX to value at address I + VX
- FX25: Store VX at address I
- FX33: Store BCD of VX at I, I+1, I+2
- FX55: Store registers V0-VX at I
- FX65: Load registers V0-VX from I
- 00EE: Return from subroutine
- 00EF: Stop emulation
- The random instruction (often 0x00 or 0x0000 in some variants, but usually handled as a specific opcode if applicable, or just the standard 35).

Implement the sprite drawing (DXYN) with XOR and collision detection in VF.
Handle the timers (delay and sound) counting down at 60Hz.","path":"chip8_ollama-gemma4-31b_01.html"}
